records.title: Guidelines for Incremental Measurement in Commerce Media
use_for: which method fits which business need
records.scope: Commerce media; the engine applies it to any channel mix
records.uncertainty: Written for commerce media; the engine generalises it. PDF read at https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/IAB_and_IAB_Europe_Guidelines_Incremental_Measurement_Commerce_Media_November_2025.pdf.
records.verification_note: Read live 2026-09-29: Full PDF read: four method families with causal strength - experiment-based (RCTs, holdouts or ghost ads, matched markets) Strong; model-based counterfactual (synthetic control, ML propensity) Strong to Moderate; econometric (MMM, time-series) Moderate to Weak; hybrid proxies (new-to-brand, baseline vs exposed, platform-reported incrementality, simple MTA) Weak. A fit matrix rates strong, conditional or limited fit per business need; MMM designed for budget allocation; experiments the gold standard for proving causal lift. Causal claims need a credible counterfactual, control of bias and separation of signal from noise (explicit identification assumptions, confounder controls, intervals excluding zero). High-stakes decisions use stronger causal methods; proxies acceptable for tactical optimisation if their limits are acknowledged.
